title: Infra GPU Fleet, Capacity, CI/CD & IaC Playbook
author: Avery Chen
body:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates best practices, runbooks, Terraform/IaC patterns, CI/CD pipeline configurations, and operational procedures for Redwood's GPU fleet, capacity planning, and related infra. It is intended for infra engineers, SREs, and platform owners responsible for provisioning, scaling, and operating GPU-backed inference clusters across clouds and on-prem environments.

Scope:
- GPU fleet lifecycle: procurement, onboarding, tagging, decommissioning
- Capacity planning and forecasting for hosted and dedicated offerings
- Terraform module patterns, versioning, and testing for GPU infrastructure
- CI/CD for infra changes: pipelines, gating, and canary strategies
- Runbooks for common operational tasks and incident playbooks

Owners and Contacts:
- Primary owner: Infra / GPU Fleet Team (eng-infra)
- Secondary owner: Platform SRE (eng-sre)
- Oncall escalation: infra-oncall@redwood-inference.internal
- Hardware procurement lead: Marcus Li (vendor liaison)

Key concepts and definitions:
- Node: an instance with one or more GPUs managed by our orchestration layer
- GPU pool: logical grouping of nodes (e.g., rtx-a6000-prod, h100-dedicated)
- Capacity unit (CU): normalized compute unit used in forecasts (1 CU ~= 1 A100-80GB v2-equivalent)
- Reserved capacity: long-lived Dedicated pools with SLA-backed throughput guarantees

Capacity planning and SLOs:
- Target utilization: 60-75% average weekly utilization per GPU pool (buffer for burst)
- Headroom policy: maintain >= 25% spare CU for 30-minute peak burst window per region
- Scale-up time objective: 10 minutes for autoscaling new nodes; 99th percentile must be <= 20 minutes
- Cost guardrails: target $/CU-hour defined per pool and tracked in Console cost dashboards

Forecasting process (quarterly and rolling 30-day):
1) Collect signals: historical utilization, active routes, expected customer rollouts, experiments
2) Convert expected workload to CU demand (use conversion table below)
3) Add safety buffer: +25% for 30-day rolling, +40% for quarterly planning
4) Submit capacity change request and procurement plan 6-8 weeks prior to need if physical procurement required

Conversion table (example):
- small-embeddings job ~ 0.05 CU / hour
- medium-chat session ~ 0.2 CU / hour
- high-throughput generation (long-seq) ~ 0.8-1.2 CU / hour

GPU inventory and tagging standard:
- Tag keys: cost_center, pool, region, hw_generation, purchase_order, lifecycle_owner
- Example tags: {cost_center: "redwood-core", pool: "h100-prod-us-west", hw_generation: "h100-v2"}
- Immutable fields: purchase_order (set at provision), lifecycle_owner

Terraform / IaC patterns:
- Module layout: use small, focused modules (networking, instance, gpu-driver, autoscaler)
- Module versioning: semver (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH). Breaking changes must increment MAJOR and require a migration plan
- State management: one statefile per environment+region+pool (e.g., infra-prod-us-west-h100.tfstate)
- Secrets: do NOT store secrets in tfstate; use KMS-wrapped provider secrets and Vault dynamic credentials

Recommended module inputs (minimal):
- region (string)
- pool_name (string)
- gpu_type (string)
- node_count_min (number)
- node_count_max (number)
- instance_profile_arn (string)

Example Terraform snippet (pseudo):
resource "redwood_gpu_node" "pool" {
  pool_name       = var.pool_name
  gpu_type        = var.gpu_type
  instance_type   = var.instance_type
  min_count       = var.node_count_min
  max_count       = var.node_count_max
  tags            = merge(var.common_tags, { pool = var.pool_name })
}

Module testing and CI:
- Required checks on merge to main for infra modules:
  1) terraform fmt && validate
  2) static checks (tfsec, checkov)
  3) unit tests for module logic (terratest)
  4) integration plan lock: run terraform plan against ephemeral test environment and store plan artifact
- Merge gating: all checks must pass + 1 approver from infra team + security signoff for networking changes

CI/CD pipeline pattern for infra changes:
Stages:
1) lint-and-static-scan (tfsec, checkov, tflint)
2) unit-test (terratest / go tests)
3) plan (against sandbox account using ephemeral credentials)
4) security-approval (automated ticket to security if networking/KMS changes are detected)
5) apply-staging (manual approval required for staging apply)
6) smoke-tests (run a smoke suite that validates node provisioning and driver installation)
7) canary-apply-production (apply to 5% of pools or a single non-critical region)
8) full-apply-production (manual approval)

CI gating rules:
- No direct pushes to main: PR-only flow
- Changes that affect state migration or destructive updates require a recorded runbook and two approvers
- Production apply requires a release window and oncall present (infra-oncall)

Canary and rollback strategy:
- Canary scope: single pool or region, up to 5% of capacity
- Smoke checks post-apply: node registration, driver health, CUDA tests, inference pipeline connection
- Rollback steps: terraform rollback using saved plan, or scale down new pool and reattach traffic routing rules to previous pools

Runbooks (common operational workflows):
1) Scale up GPU pool quickly (urgent demand)
   - Owner: infra-oncall
   - Steps:
     1. Verify demand spike in Console and confirm with product/CS if external event (5m)
     2. If autoscaler is healthy: temporarily increase node_count_max for the pool via emergency terraform variable override and apply
     3. If autoscaler unavailable: manually provision nodes via cloud console using standard tags and run the GPU bootstrap script (link to bootstrap repo)
     4. Verify nodes register with cluster manager and pass health checks (count and readiness)
     5. Monitor 30 minutes for stability; if stable, convert emergency override into IaC change and follow standard PR flow

2) Replace faulty GPU host (hardware fault)
   - Owner: infra-hardware
   - Steps:
     1. Drain the node from scheduler (cordon + drain)
     2. Tag node as failed: lifecycle_state=failed, hardware_ticket=<id>
     3. Provision replacement node from same pool with same tags
     4. Run health and CUDA validation, then uncordon
     5. File RMA with vendor and attach logs to ticket

3) Terraform state conflict / lock recovery
   - Owner: infra-iac
   - Steps:
     1. Identify lock holder using backend (e.g., S3/DynamoDB or remote backend API)
     2. Contact the locking user or, if stale (> 60m) follow the emergency unlock procedure documented in the IaC repo
     3. After unlock, re-run plan and verify no pending destructive diffs

Operational checklists before major pool changes:
- Confirm backups of tfstate and snapshot AMIs exist
- Verify rollback plan and smoke tests are staged in CI
- Notify downstream owners and CS with planned maintenance window
- Reserve extra capacity in adjacent pools for immediate fallback

Observability and alerting:
- Must have dashboards for: per-pool utilization, per-model token throughput, per-instance GPU memory pressure, driver crash rates
- Alerts to create:
  - high-utilization-alert: trigger at 85% 15m sustained per pool
  - driver-crash-rate: trigger if >3 crashes per node / hour
  - node-provision-failure: trigger if node not ready after 15 minutes post-provision

Security considerations and network topology:
- GPU instances must be launched in private subnets with NAT for outbound software downloads
- Bastion + session manager for interactive access; no direct public SSH
- KMS keys: use separate CMKs per environment (prod/staging) and rotate annually

Post-change verification (smoke test checklist):
- Node registers in fleet manager and autoscaler sees correct capacity
- Drivers and CUDA tests pass (sample bench run)
- Latency SLOs measured for a small synthetic workload within expected bounds
- Cost/usage metrics reported to Console Cost Dashboard

Appendices:
A) Troubleshooting commands (examples):
- Check node registration: fleetctl nodes list --pool h100-prod-us-west
- CUDA health: ssh <node> sudo /opt/gputools/cuda-health-check.sh
- Terraform plan using ephemeral workspace: ./ci/run-terraform-plan.sh --workspace sandbox-us-west

B) Links:
- IaC repo: git@github.com:redwood-inference/infra-iac.git
- Bootstrap scripts: git@github.com:redwood-inference/gpu-bootstrap.git
- GPU runbook (legacy): /confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/gpu-capacity-and-infra-runbook-2026

C) Change log:
